previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: Mr. ___ was admitted with acute hypercarbic respiratory failure due to tracheal occlusion from a fibrous clot, occurring the day after a prior discharge. He has a complex history of Ruvalcaba-Myhre-Smith syndrome and relapsing polychondritis with recurrent tracheal stenosis, requiring multiple prior dilations and a tracheostomy. He underwent urgent bronchoscopy and tracheal dilation, which relieved the obstruction. His elevated white count and lactate improved with supportive care and antibiotics. An acid-fast bacillus was cultured from BAL, but TB was ruled out; etanercept was held pending further evaluation. He was treated with a course of Augmentin, started on a prednisone taper, and maintained on Bactrim prophylaxis. A swallow study showed mild oropharyngeal dysphagia without aspiration, allowing return to baseline diet. He was discharged home with services on a steroid taper, antibiotics, and instructions to restart methotrexate after antibiotic completion.

IP Procedure:
Procedure:The procedure, indications, preparation and potential 
complications were explained to the patient, who indicated his 
understanding and signed the corresponding consent forms. A 
standard time out was performed as per protocol. The procedure 
was performed for diagnostic purposes at the operating room. A 
physical exam was performed. The bronchoscope was introduced 
through a tracheostomy stoma and advanced under direct 
visualization until the tracheobronchial tree was reached.The 
procedure was not difficult. The quality of the preparation was 
good. The patient tolerated the procedure well. There were no 
complications.
other findings:Procedure: Flexible bronchoscopy with aspiration 
of secretions and balloon dilation of trachea and LMS. On airway 
examination, the trachea was noted to be narrowed and the 
therapeutic scope could not be passed without difficulty. Due to 
concern of causing injury to the airway mucosa, it was balloon 
dilated initially to 8 mm. With this we could pass by this 
narrowing and visualized the carina. The LMS was pinhole. The 
RMS was relatively patent and we could pass the therapeutic 
scope. We then balloon dilated the LMS to 10 mm with improved 
patency. The LUL and LLL segments were identified. Lastly we 
balloon dilated the trachea to 12 mm with improved patency. 
Mucosal bleeding was treated with topical iced epinephrine and 
lidocaine.
Impression:Tracheal and LMS narrowing s/p balloon dilation
